sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].

The path was cyclical rather than steady: a 20.4% jump in FY2018 to $54.7 billion [F3][D92], a 22.4% collapse in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], then a 12.8% rise in FY2023 to $67.1 billion [F8][D357].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory changes across all three primary segments [P59].

The FY2023 gain was primarily favorable price realization and higher sales volume [P32], while FY2025's 4.3% growth to $67.6 billion [F10][D463] reflected higher volume partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P13].
In FY2025 Power & Energy was the largest segment at 47.6% of revenue [D757], contributing 5.2pp of growth [D759], while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D765][D766].
Construction Industries' decline was primarily unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume [P8].
Operating income grew far faster than revenue over the window, at a 28.6% CAGR against 6.4% [F202][F201], but in FY2025 operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue [D489].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% in FY2025 [D467] against a 17.7% net income decline [D465], as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
The FY2025 profit decline was mainly unfavorable manufacturing costs and price realization, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P17].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 [F30] sat above the 14.3% window median [D1123] but well below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F29][D1122].
The FY2025 margin fell 3.7pp [D476], with cost of revenue subtracting 4.2pp [D490] while SG&A and R&D were roughly neutral [D491][D492].
That cost-of-revenue pressure was unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion, largely from higher tariffs, plus $817 million of unfavorable price realization [P9].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% [F50] sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin [F30], with a 24.0% effective tax rate [D449] and $892 million of other income [X110].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion [F80] covered net income 1.32x in FY2025 [D450], and free cash flow of $8.9 billion [F100] matched net income at 1.00x [D451].
Free cash flow margin of 13.2% [D447] was above the 11.9% window median [D1129] but below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D1128].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion in FY2025 [F90][D470], 4.2% of revenue [D446] and 1.25x D&A [D452].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash rose on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes, partly offset by lower profit [P4].
Net debt stood at $26.2 billion in FY2025 [D456], with cash of $10.0 billion [F140] and total debt of $36.2 billion [D455].
That net-cash ratio ranked at the 43rd percentile against a -35.6% industrials peer median (n=7) [D1151][D1152], and the current ratio was 1.44x [F180].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion and dividends of $2.7 billion [X140][X150] used 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% [D462] ranked at the 100th percentile against a 23.3% peer median (n=6) [D1155][D1156].
Net debt rose for a second year, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D350] to $24.9 billion in FY2024 [D403] and $26.2 billion in FY2025 [D456].
Leverage is still modest against equity of $21.3 billion [F200], but the direction removes the balance-sheet cushion that funded prior buybacks.
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 to $64.8 billion [F9][D410] before recovering 4.3% in FY2025 [D463].
The dip looks cyclical rather than structural, since FY2025 volume growth offset price weakness [P13].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to margins and ratios but matters where precision is claimed.
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the 14.3% window median [D1123] or falls toward the 16.5% FY2025 level [F30], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether capex stays above the 4.2% of revenue reached in FY2025 [D446] or falls back toward the 3.1% FY2024 level [D393], reported in the FY2026 cash flow statement.
Whether net debt exceeds the $26.2 billion FY2025 level [D456] or reverses toward the $22.1 billion FY2023 level [D350], reported in the FY2026 balance sheet.
